newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-INDY 500 POSTPONED TO MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-INDY 500 POSTPONED TO MONDAY.

text.p: The Indy 500 was postponed Sunday because of heavy rain and has been rescheduled to run Monday morning, race stewards said.
Keith Ward, chief steward of the United States Auto Club, announced the postponement of the 81st running of the classic American auto race some 2-1/2 hours after its scheduled start.
Ward called off the race once there was no longer enough time for the track dry to be able to complete the race. He rescheduled it for 11 a.m. local time (1600 gmt) Monday.
It was the fifth staging of the 500 mile (804 km) race around the four-turn, 2.5 mile (4 km) circuit which had to be postponed due to rain.
Races previously postponed before they could be started due to rain were in 1915 and 1986 (when there were two separate postponements).
The race was interrupted by rain and resumed on a later day in 1967 and 1973 (when it was restarted on two following days and then shortened to 133 laps because of rain interrupting the third try).
Other rain-shortened races were in 1926, 1950, 1975 and 1976.
Wet tracks increase the danger of cars crashing into concrete walls that ring the Indy car ovals.
